celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ وَالطَّارِقِ﴾: originally, anyone who comes by night; from this are the stars, because they rise at night.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ﴾ — made you know — ﴿مَا الطَّارِقُ﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the second object of «أدرى»; and what comes after the first «ما» is its khabar. In it is a magnifying of the matter of the ṭāriq, which is explained by what follows it: it is

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿النَّجْمُ﴾, that is, the Pleiades or any star, ﴿الثَّاقِبُ﴾: the shining, because it pierces the darkness with its light. And the answer to the oath is:

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ﴾: with «ما» lightened, it is redundant (mazīda), and «إن» is lightened (mukhaffafa) from the heavy «إنّ», its noun being omitted, that is, «إنه», and the lām is the differentiating lām (fāriqa). With it doubled [لَمَّا], «إن» is negating (nāfiya) and «لمّا» means «إلا» ("except"). The guardian is from the angels; he guards its deeds, good and evil.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ with a look of reflection ﴿مِمَّ خُلِقَ﴾: from what thing. Its answer:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿خُلِقَ مِنْ مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ﴾: possessing a gushing forth, from the man and the woman, into her womb,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَيْنِ الصُّلْبِ﴾ of the man ﴿وَالتَّرَائِبِ﴾ of the woman, which are the bones of the chest.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ — He, Exalted is He — ﴿عَلَى رَجْعِهِ﴾ — raising man after his death — ﴿لَقَادِرٌ﴾. So when he reflects on his origin, he knows that the One able to do that is able to raise him.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تُبْلَى﴾: are tested and laid bare ﴿السَّرَائِرُ﴾: the hidden things of the hearts in beliefs and intentions.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فَمَا لَهُ﴾ — the one who denies the Resurrection — ﴿مِنْ قُوَّةٍ﴾ by which to protect himself from the punishment ﴿وَلَا نَاصِرٍ﴾ to ward it off from him.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ﴾: the rain, because it returns time after time,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾: the splitting open for plants.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ﴾: it separates truth from falsehood,

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿يَكِيدُونَ كَيْدًا﴾: they devise plots against the Prophet ﷺ,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَأَكِيدُ كَيْدًا﴾: I lead them on step by step from where they do not know.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿فَمَهِّلِ﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿الْكَافِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ﴾: a tawkīd (emphasis) made graceful by the difference in wording; that is, give them respite ﴿رُوَيْدًا﴾: a little. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasizing the meaning of the governing word (ʿāmil), the diminutive of «رود» or of «إرواد» by way of tarkhīm (truncation). Allah the Exalted seized them at Badr, and the respite was abrogated by the Verse of the Sword, that is, the command to fight and wage jihad.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿وَالسَّماءِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم" (I swear); ﴿وَالطَّارِقِ﴾: conjoined to السماء.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause ما أدراك… is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مَا الطَّارِقُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿النَّجْمُ﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو"; ﴿الثَّاقِبُ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾: a particle of negation; ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), muḍāf to نفس; ﴿لَمَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿عَلَيْها حافِظٌ﴾: fronted khabar (predicate) and postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of كل, and the clause إن… is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿خُلِقَ﴾: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿خُلِقَ﴾: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿مِنْ ماءٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿دافِقٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ماء; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿يَخْرُجُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of ماء; ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الصُّلْبِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿وَالتَّرائِبِ﴾: conjoined to it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿عَلى رَجْعِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿لَقادِرٌ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and قادر is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿تُبْلَى﴾: a passive imperfect verb; ﴿السَّرائِرُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿فَما﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿لَهُ﴾: fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ﴿قُوَّةٍ﴾: genitive in form, nominative in position, the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿لا﴾ is negative; ﴿ناصِرٍ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَالسَّماءِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم" (I swear); ﴿ذاتِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of السماء; ﴿الرَّجْعِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:12-12.t: The clause is conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is the same.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَقَوْلٌ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿قول﴾ is its khabar (predicate); ﴿فَصْلٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative, working like laysa; ﴿هُوَ﴾: its noun; ﴿بِالْهَزْلِ﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and ﴿الهزل﴾ is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿يَكِيدُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿كَيْداً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وَأَكِيدُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿كَيْداً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿فَمَهِّلِ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْكافِرِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis of a condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَمْهِلْهُمْ﴾: an imperative verb and its object, the agent being latent; ﴿رُوَيْداً﴾: naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is a tawkīd (emphasis) of what precedes it.

farraa:1-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلطَّارِقِ﴾.
الطارق: the star, because it rises at night; whatever comes to you at night is a طارق. Then He explained it and said: ﴿النَّجْمُ الثَّاقِبُ﴾. الثاقب: the shining one. The Arabs say to the one kindling a fire: أثقب نارك (make your fire blaze). It is also said that الثاقب is the star called Zuḥal (Saturn); and الثاقب is the one that has risen above the stars. The Arabs say of a bird when it reaches the belly of the sky in height: قد ثقّب. All of that has come in the exegesis.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا﴾.
The general public read it "لمّا", and some read it lightened; al-Kisāʾī used to read it lightened. We do not know the rationale for the doubled form, and we consider it a dialect of Hudhayl, who use (لمّا) for إلا together with the lightened إنْ, and do not go beyond that. As though He said [«قالك» in the source]: there is no soul but that over it [134/b] there is a guardian.
Whoever reads it lightened says: it is only the lām of the response to إنْ, and the (ما) after it is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant), as in His saying: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ ميثاقهم﴾. He says: so there is no doubling in (ما) when it is a ṣila.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ﴾.
The guardian from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, guards it until He hands it over to the decrees [of fate].

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِن مَّآءٍ دَافِقٍ﴾.
The people of the Hijaz do this more than others: making the passive [participle] active when it is used as an adjective, as in the Arabs' saying: هذا سرٌّ كاتم (a concealing secret, i.e. a concealed secret), همٌّ ناصبٌ (a toiling care, i.e. a wearying care), ليلٌ نائمٌ (a sleeping night) and عيشةٌ راضيةٌ (a pleased life, i.e. a pleasing life). What helped this is that it agrees with the verse-endings that it accompanies.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِن بَيْنِ ٱلصُّلْبِ وَٱلتَّرَآئِبِ﴾.
He means: from the backbone and the breastbones. It is permissible to say of two things: ليخرجنّ من بين هذين خير كثير (much good will come forth from between these two), and من هذين (from these two). الصلب: the man's backbone; الترائب: what surrounds the upper chest of the woman, where the necklaces lie.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ﴾.
He is indeed able to bring man back after death.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And Mindal narrated to me from Layth from Mujāhid, who said: He is indeed able to return the fluid into the urethra.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلرَّجْعِ﴾.
It begins with rain, then returns with it every year.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلأَرْضِ ذَاتِ ٱلصَّدْعِ﴾.
It splits open with plants.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: His saying «والطارق»: a noun conjoined to «السماء».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The wāw is resumptive; «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «أدراك» is the khabar (predicate); and the clause «ما الطارق» is the second object of «أدراك».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «النجم» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هو الطارق (it is al-ṭāriq). [Translator's note: so in the source; the omitted mubtadaʾ هو refers to الطارق.]

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam); «إن» is negating; «كل» is mubtadaʾ (subject); «لمَّا»: a particle of restriction meaning إلا (except); and the clause «عليها حافظ» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «كل».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The fāʾ is resumptive, and the lām is that of command; «مِمَّ» is composed of the genitive preposition «مِنْ» and the interrogative «ما» whose alif has been dropped, in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلق»; and the clause «خلق» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «يخرج» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {مَاءٍ}.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (إنه على رجعه لقادر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive, and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «قوة» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the preposition «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate)

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: (إنه لقول فصل) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam)

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: (وما هو بالهزل) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ}, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: (إنهم يكيدون كيدا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: (وأكيد كيدا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya)

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: (فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive, and the clause «أمهلهم» is resumptive, emphasizing the preceding clause; «رويدا»: nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object), synonymous with its governing word, and it is the diminutive of «إرْواد» by curtailment (tarkhīm).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying, the Exalted: (إن كل نفس لما عليها): whoever reads (لما) without doubling makes (ما) redundant (zāʾida) and (إن) lightened from the heavy one; what follows it is nominative because of its deficiency [i.e. having lost its governing force]. It is the answer to the oath, as if He said "every soul — over it is surely a guardian"; its proper form is "over every soul there is surely a guardian". So (حافظ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (لعليها) is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of (كل). The lām entered and is obligatory to distinguish between the (إن) lightened from the heavy one and the (إن) meaning negating (ما). Whoever doubles (لما) makes (لما) mean (إلا) and (إن) mean (ما), its implied form being "There is no soul but that over it is a guardian". Sībawayh reported (نشدتك الله لما فعلت), i.e. "I adjure you by Allah, only do (إلا فعلت)".

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (يوم تبلى السرائر): (يوم) is an adverbial, and its governor is (لقادر). (رجعه) does not govern it, because you would then be separating the ṣila (relative clause) from its relative [i.e. the maṣdar from what it governs] by the khabar (predicate) of (إن). This is according to the view of whoever says that (رجعه) means His resurrecting him and reviving him after his death. As for whoever says (رجعه) means returning the water into the urethra, or says returning the old man to his states from the sperm-drop, or holding back the water so that it does not come out of the urethra, he makes (يوما) accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "remember the day when [secrets] are tested"; (لقادر) does not govern it [on this view], because He did not mean that He is able to return the water into the urethra and the rest on the Day of Resurrection; He only informed that He is able to do it in this world, were He to will it.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿والسماء والطارق﴾: the wāw: a particle of oath and genitive. Wa-l-samāʾ: genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of oath. Wa-l-ṭāriq: also sworn by, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is parenthetical, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. Mā is an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: adrā is an imperfect verb [Translator's note: so in the source; adrā is a past verb], nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ما﴾.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿الطارق﴾: khabar of the second ﴿ما﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿ما الطارق﴾ stands in place of the second and third objects of ﴿أدراك﴾. The clause ﴿وما أدراك...﴾ is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿النجم﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, i.e. "huwa al-najmu al-thāqib" (it is the piercing star); the clause is parenthetical between the oath and its answer, like the one before it. Or: a badal (substitute) from ﴿الطارق﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الثاقب﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿النجم﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿إن﴾: (read) without doubling (in), a negative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿كل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿نفس﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿لما﴾: (read) with doubling (lammā), meaning illā, for restriction (ḥaṣr); a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿عليها﴾: ʿalā: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and ﴿ها﴾: a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿حافظ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of ﴿كل﴾, and the clause ﴿إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فلينظر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the lām of command is a particle indeclinable on the sukūn; and yanẓur is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn.
﴿الإنسان﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿ممَّ﴾: min is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and ﴿مَ﴾ is an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn on the alif, which is dropped because the preposition has entered upon it, in the position of the genitive by ﴿من﴾; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلق﴾.
﴿خلق﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa". The clause ﴿خلق﴾ is in the place of the accusative by His saying ﴿فلينظر﴾, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from it by the interrogative.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿خلق﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".
﴿من﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿ماء﴾: a noun in the genitive by min, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلق﴾.
﴿دافق﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ماء﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra. The clause ﴿خلق...﴾ is resumptive by way of explanation (istiʾnāf bayānī), with no grammatical position, or a badal (substitute) from ﴿خلق﴾ in the previous ayah.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿يخرج﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".
﴿من﴾: a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿بين﴾: an adverb, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿الصلب﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿والترائب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and al-tarāʾib is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to al-ṣulb, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿إنه﴾: inna is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle for emphasis and the accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna, referring to Allah.
﴿على﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿رجعه﴾: a noun in the genitive by ﴿على﴾, the sign of the genitive being the kasra, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قادر﴾.
﴿لقادر﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) is a particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, and ﴿قادر﴾ is khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قادر﴾.
﴿تبلى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.
﴿السرائر﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿تبلى السرائر﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿فما﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and mā is negative, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿له﴾: the lām is a preposition indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿من﴾: a connective (ṣila) preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿قوة﴾: a noun genitive by min in form and nominative by position, because it is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and ﴿لا﴾ is negative, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿ناصر﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿قوة﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿والسماء﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and al-samāʾ: a noun in the genitive by the wāw of the oath, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of oath.
﴿ذات﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿السماء﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿الرجع﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿والأرض﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿السماء﴾.
﴿ذات﴾: an adjective (ṣifa), genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿الصدع﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿إنه﴾: inna is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle for emphasis and the accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿لقول﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) is a particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, and it is for emphasis; ﴿قول﴾ is khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿فصل﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قول﴾. The clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative mā, which works like laysa; it is a negative particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿هو﴾: a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿بالهزل﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿الهزل﴾ is the predicate (khabar) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by position and genitive by the bāʾ in form.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿إنهم﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; inna is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle for emphasis and the accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of ﴿إن﴾; and the mīm is a particle of the plural, indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿يكيدون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent). The clause yakīdūn is khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿كيدًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وأكيد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and ﴿أكيد﴾ is an imperfect verb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿يكيدون﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿كيدا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿فمهل﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and mahhil is an imperative verb indeclinable on the sukūn; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta".
﴿الكافرين﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿أمهلهم﴾: an imperative verb indeclinable on the sukūn; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta"; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; and the mīm is a particle of the plural, indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿رويدًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) from an unused verb, synonymous with its governing word; it is the diminutive of ﴿إرْواد﴾ by way of truncation (tarkhīm), and it is accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: وَالسَّماءِ is genitive by the wāw of oath. وَالطَّارِقِ is conjoined to it; [it is] from their saying طرق طروقا, when one comes by night.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: The exegetes hold that it [الرجع] is the rain, because it returns every year — except Ibn Zayd, who said: وَالسَّماءِ ذاتِ الرَّجْعِ — its sun, its moon and its stars. The plural of رجع is رجعان, heard from the Arabs, not according to analogy; if analogy were followed, one would say أرجع and رجوع.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: [ذاتِ الصَّدْعِ,] because it splits open with plants.

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: [إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ is] the answer to the second oath, i.e. possessing decisiveness; and likewise وَما هُوَ بِالْهَزْلِ (14).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: That is, against the Prophet ﷺ and the believers.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: [رُوَيْداً is] a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. a gentle respite. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās about «رويدا»: he said: He is saying: near [in time]. Al-Ḥasan said: a little.

nahhas-irab:2-3.t:
النَّجْمُ is in the sense of "it is the piercing star". It is also possible that الثَّاقِبُ is a naʿt (adjective) of الطارق. The soundest that has been said about the meaning of الثاقب is what Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās about الثاقب: he said:
He is saying: the shining one. Al-Farrāʾ reported: ثقب means "it rose high", and that it is Saturn; it was called الثاقب because of its height. Someone else said: [it was so called] because of its rising from the east, as though it pierces its place.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī. Abū Jaʿfar and al-Ḥasan read إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ (4). [Translator's note: the source prints both readings as «لَمَّا»; the undoubled mīm of the first is supplied according to the explanation that follows.] Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading is clear in Arabic: ما is redundant (zāʾida) and «إن» is lightened from the heavy [إنّ]; this is the school of Sībawayh, and it is the answer to the oath. In the second reading «لمّا» has the sense of "except": [no soul but has] over it [a guardian]. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh reported: أقسمت عليك لمّا فعلت, meaning "I adjure you, [do nothing] but do it". [Translator's note: the source glosses this as «ألا فعلت», apparently for «إلا فعلت».]

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: [فَلْيَنْظُرِ is] from the seeing of the heart. The original is فَلِيَنظر; the kasra [of the lām] was dropped because of its heaviness, the verb is jussive by the lām of command, and the rāʾ takes a kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. مِمَّ خُلِقَ: the original is مِمّا; the alif was dropped because it is interrogative. The statement is complete [here].

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ is that the meaning of دافق is مدفوق (poured out). He [al-Farrāʾ] said: The people of the Ḥijāz are those who do this most: they bring فاعل in the sense of مفعول when it is a naʿt (adjective), as in «ماء دافق» and سرّ كاتم, i.e. a concealed (مكتوم) secret. Abū Jaʿfar said: فاعل in the sense of مفعول destroys clarity; it is not sound and not subject to analogy. If this were permissible, ضارب ("striker") would be permissible in the sense of مضروب ("struck"). The view of the Basrans is that it is on [the pattern of] relation (nasab), as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 555- كليني لهم يا أميمة ناصب (Leave me, O Umayma, to a wearisome care), and as [another] said: [al-ṭawīl] 556-
وليس بذي سيف فيقتلني به ... وليس بذي رمح وليس بنبّال ]
(He is not one with a sword, that he should kill me with it, nor one with a spear, nor an archer.) [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears at the end of the verse in the source.]

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
ʿĪsā read مِنْ بَيْنِ الصُّلُبِ [Translator's note: the source prints «الصُّلْبِ», the standard reading; ʿĪsā's variant is presumably «الصُّلُب», as the following remark suggests.], and al-Aṣmaʿī reported: الصُّلُب is in the sense of الصُّلْب.
وَالتَّرائِبِ is the plural of تريبة [Translator's note: the source reads «تربية», a misprint]; one also says تريب. The scholars differed about its meaning. Among the soundest that has been said about it is what ʿAṭiyya related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الترائب is the place of the necklace. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الترائب is [what is] between the woman's breasts. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: الترائب are the ribs down to the bottom of the backbone. Mujāhid said: what is between the shoulders and the chest. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الترائب are the hands, the feet and the eyes. Qatāda said: الترائب is towards the backbone. Al-Layth ibn Saʿd related from Maʿmar ibn Abī Ḥabība, who said: الترائب is the freshness (marrow) of the heart, and from it comes the child. Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are not contradictory, because it is related that the fluid comes out from the whole body, even from every hair; but the first view is the one used in the speech of the Arabs, as the poet said: [al-wāfir] 557-
ومن ذهب يلوح على تريب ... كلون العاج ليس بذي غضون
(And of gold gleaming on an upper breast, like the colour of ivory, without wrinkles.)
And as [another] said: [al-ṭawīl] 558-
مهفهفة بيضاء غير مفاضة ... ترائبها مصقولة كالسّجنجل
(Slender-waisted, fair, not flabby-bellied, her breastbones polished like a mirror.)
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the meaning of "between the backbone and the breastbones" is "from the backbone and the breastbones"; he does not make بين redundant, but [it is] as one says: فلان هالك بين هذين ("so-and-so is perishing between these two").

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
The scholars differed about this pronoun. Among the soundest that has been said about it is the view of Qatāda, who said: [He is able] to resurrect him and bring him back; on this [view] the pronoun is for man. Abū Jaʿfar said: It was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, from Yaḥyā ibn Ziyād, from Mindal ibn ʿAlī, from Layth, from Mujāhid, concerning إِنَّهُ عَلى رَجْعِهِ لَقادِرٌ: he said: [able] to return the fluid into the urethra. This is the school of Ibn Zayd; he said: على رجعه لقادر — able to hold it back so that it does not come out. These are two views, and from al-Ḍaḥḥāk [something] like their meaning; and from him a third view: على رجعه لقادر — he said: [able] to return him after old age to youth, after youth to childhood, and after childhood to the sperm-drop. Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is the clearer of them; Muḥammad ibn Jarīr chose it, except that he used an argument to strengthen it which is a mistake in Arabic. He claimed that His saying, the Exalted, يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرائِرُ belongs to the ṣila (completion) of رجعه, interpreting it as "He is able to bring him back on the day the secrets are tested". Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is a mistake. If it were so, it would enter into the ṣila of رجعه, and you would be separating the ṣila from what it completes by the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and that is not permissible. Rather, «يوم» is governed by ناصر.

nahhas-irab:9-10.t:
[تُبْلَى means] they are tested and made manifest. It was said: it means the prayer, the fasting and the ritual bath after major impurity.
فَما لَهُ مِنْ قُوَّةٍ: Qatāda said: [no] strength to protect him from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; وَلا ناصِرٍ to help him against Him. Al-Thawrī said: مِنْ قُوَّةٍ — of kinsfolk; وَلا ناصِرٍ — an ally.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {والطارق}: al-ṭāriq is originally the active participle of ṭaraqa yaṭruqu ṭurūqan, i.e. he came by night. [The poet] said:
4539 - فمِثْلَكِ حُبْلى قد طَرَقْتُ ومُرْضِعاً ... فألهَيْتُها عن ذي تمائمَ مُحْوِلِ
(Many a woman like you, pregnant or nursing, have I visited by night, and distracted her from her year-old infant wearing amulets.)
Its origin is from striking. Al-ṭāriq bi-l-ḥaṣā is the one who strikes with pebbles [for divination]. [The poet] said:
4540 - لعَمْرُكَ ما تَدْري الضواربُ بالحصى ... ولا زاجراتُ الطيرِ ما اللَّهُ صانعُ
(By your life, neither the women who strike pebbles nor those who drive off birds [for omens] know what Allah will do.)
Then its use was extended, and everyone who comes by night was called ṭāriq.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا}: the light and the doubled forms of «لَمَّاً» were discussed in Sūrat Hūd. For whoever reads it light here, «إنْ» here is lightened from the heavy [inna] (mukhaffafa), «كلُّ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), «عليها» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «حافظٌ» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of «كل», with «ما» redundant (zāʾida) after the distinguishing lām. Alternatively «عليها» alone may be the khabar, with «حافِظٌ» as its agent (fāʿil), which is better. Alternatively «كلُّ» may be a mubtadaʾ and «حافظٌ» its khabar, with «عليها» attached to it and «ما» also redundant. All of this branches from the view of the Basrans. The Kufans said: «إنْ» here is negative, the lām means «إلاَّ» (except), affirming after the negation, and «ما» is redundant. The discussion of this was given in full before.
As for the reading with doubling, «إنْ» is negative and «لَمَّا» means «إلاَّ»; the evidence for that was given in full in Hūd. Hārūn reported that «إنَّ» was read here with doubling and «كلَّ» in the accusative as its noun, the lām being the one that enters the predicate, «ما» redundant and «حافظٌ» its khabar. On every analysis, «إنْ» and what falls in its domain is the reply to the oath, whether one makes it the lightened form or the negative. It has also been said: the reply is {إِنَّهُ على رَجْعِهِ}, and what lies between is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ); but this is far-fetched.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {دَافِقٍ}: it has been said: it is fāʿil (active) in the sense of mafʿūl (passive), the reverse of their saying «سيلٌ مُفْعَم» (a filled torrent) and of the saying of the Exalted {حِجَاباً مَّسْتُوراً} [al-Isrāʾ: 45] on one view. It has also been said: «دافق» is by way of relation (nasab), i.e. possessing gushing (dafq) or outpouring (indifāq). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is valid for the water to be gushing (dāfiq), because part of it pushes (yadfuqu) another part, i.e. drives it; so some of it is gushing and some of it gushed." End of quote. Al-dafq is pouring, so its verb is transitive. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «مَدْفُوقٍ» (poured), as though he was explaining the meaning.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {والترآئب}: plural of tarība, which is the place of the necklace among the bones of the chest; because the child is created from the fluid of both of them: the man's fluid is in his loins (ṣulb) and the woman's in her breast-bones (tarāʾib). This is the meaning of his saying {مِن نُّطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ} [al-Insān: 2]. The poet said:
4540 - مُهَفْهَفَةٌ بيضاءُ غيرُ مُفاضَةٍ ... تَرائِبُها مَصْقُولةٌ كالسَّجَنْجَلِ
(Slender-waisted, fair, not paunchy, her breast-bones polished like a mirror.)
[Translator's note: the verse number 4540 is as printed; it repeats the number of an earlier verse.]
And he said:
4541 - والزَّعْفَرانُ على ترائبِها ... شَرِقَتْ به اللَّبَّاتُ والنَّحْرُ
(And saffron on her breast-bones, with which the upper chest and the throat are steeped.)
Abū ʿUbayda said: "The plural of tarība is tarīb." [The poet] said:
4542 - ومِنْ ذَهَبٍ يَذُوْبُ على تَرِيْبٍ ... كلَوْنِ العاجِ ليس بذي غُضونِ
(And of gold melting upon a breast the colour of ivory, without wrinkles.)
It has also been said: al-tarāʾib are the collarbones. It has also been said: the ribs of the man which are below the loins. It has also been said: what lies between the shoulders and the chest. From Ibn ʿAbbās: they are a person's extremities: his hands, his feet and his eyes. It has also been said: the essence of the heart. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In these views there is arbitrariness regarding the language."
The majority read «يَخْرُج» in the active voice, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ibn Miqsam in the passive. He also, and the people of Mecca, read «الصُّلُب» with ḍamma on the ṣād and the lām, and al-Yamānī with fatḥa on both; on this is the saying of al-ʿAjjāj:
4543 - في صَلَبٍ مِثْلِ العِنانِ المُؤْدَمِ
(In a back [ṣalab] like a rein of tanned leather.)
Its dialectal forms were given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. The strangest of them is «صالِب», as in [the poet's] saying:
4544 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . مِنْ صالِبٍ إلى رَحِمٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(… from loins [ṣālib] to womb …)

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {إِنَّهُ}: the pronoun refers to the Creator, who is indicated by his saying «خُلِقَ» (he was created), because it is known that there is no creator other than Him.
His saying: {على رَجْعِهِ}: there are two views on the hāʾ. First: it is the pronoun of man, i.e. [able] to resurrect him after his death. Second: it is the pronoun of the fluid, i.e. He returns the semen into the urethra or the loins.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تبلى}: there are several views on it. Abū al-Baqāʾ arranged them according to the disagreement over the pronoun, saying, on the view that the pronoun refers to man: "There are several views on it. First: it is governed by «قادر»." — Except that Ibn ʿAṭiyya, after reporting several views from the grammarians, said: "All these groups fled from making «لَقادِرٌ» the governing word, lest it appear from that that the power is restricted to that day alone." Then he said: "But when one reflects on the meaning and what the eloquent speech of the Arabs requires, it is permissible for «لَقادر» to be the governing word, because if He is able to do that at this time, He is all the more able at other times." — "Second: the governing word is implied, by way of clarification, i.e. He returns him on the day when [secrets] are tested. Third: its implied form is 'remember', so it would be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). On the view that it refers to the fluid, what governs it is 'remember'." End of quote, in summary.
Some allowed the governing word to be «ناصرٍ». This is invalid, because what comes after the negative «ما» and what comes after the fāʾ cannot govern what precedes them. It has also been said: what governs it is «رَجْعِه». This is invalid, because a foreign element, namely the khabar (predicate), separates the maṣdar (verbal noun) from what it governs; though some tolerate this in the case of an adverb (ẓarf).

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {ذَاتِ الرجع}: it has been said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning the return of the sun and the moon to it. It has also been said: [al-rajʿ is] rain, as in [the poet's] saying describing a sword:
4545 - أبيضُ كالرَّجْعِ رَسوبٌ إذا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Gleaming white like rain-water, sinking deep when …)
just as it was called awb (return), as in [the poet's] saying:
4546 - رَبَّاءُ شَمَّاءُ لا يَأْوي لِقُلَّتِها ... إلاَّ السَّحابُ وإلاَّ الأَوْبُ والسَّبَلُ
(A lofty, towering [peak]: nothing finds shelter on its summit but the clouds, the returning rain and the downpour.)

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {إِنَّهُ}: the reply to the oath in his saying «والسَّماءِ». Al-hazl (jest) is the opposite of seriousness and of rolling up one's sleeves in a matter. Al-Kumayt said:
4547 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يُجَدُّ بنافي كلِّ يومٍ ونَهْزِلُ
(… every day [fate] is in earnest with us, while we jest.)
The pronoun in «إنَّه» refers to the Quran. It has also been said: to the preceding speech that indicates the resurrection and the raising up.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {أَمْهِلْهُمْ}: this is the reading of the majority; since the command was repeated for emphasis, He varied the two wordings. From Ibn ʿAbbās: «مَهِّلْهُمْ», like the first. Al-imhāl and al-tamhīl mean waiting. One says: amhaltuka kadhā, i.e. I waited for you to do it. Al-mahl is gentleness and deliberateness.
His saying: {رُوَيْداً}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the meaning of the governing word; it is the diminutive of irwād, by way of truncation (tarkhīm). It has also been said: rather, it is the diminutive of «رُوْد», and he recited:
4548 - تكادُ لا تَثْلِمُ البَطْحاءُ وَطْأتَه ... كأنَّه ثَمِلٌ يَمْشي على رُوْدِ
(The sandy valley-bed scarcely shows the dent of his tread, as though he were a tipsy man walking gently.)
Know that ruwaydan is used as a maṣdar in place of uttering its verb, so it is sometimes annexed, as in his saying {فَضَرْبَ الرقاب} [Muḥammad: 4], and sometimes not annexed, as in: ruwaydan zaydan. [It is also used as a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), in which case it does not take tanwīn but is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, as in: ruwayda zaydan.] It occurs as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as in: sārū ruwaydan, i.e. going slowly; and as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, as in «ساروا رُوَيْداً», i.e. a slow journey. These rules have a place more fitting for them.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَهِّلِ الْكَافِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْدًا (١٧)).
(رُوَيْدًا): a naʿt (adjective) for an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. «إِمْهَالًا رُوَيْدًا» (a gentle respite); and «رُوَيْدًا» is the diminutive of «رُودٍ».
It is also said that it is a maṣdar with the augment omitted, the original being «إِرْوَادًا». [Translator's note: the printed text reads «مَصْدَرٌ مَحْذُوفٌ، الزِّيَادَةُ», apparently for «مَصْدَرٌ مَحْذُوفُ الزِّيَادَةِ»; translated accordingly.] And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خُلِقَ مِنْ مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ (٦)).
(دَافِقٍ): it is by way of attribution (nasab), i.e. «ذُو انْدِفَاقٍ» (possessing gushing). It is also said that it is in the sense of «مَدْفُوقٍ» (poured forth).
It is also said that it is according to the meaning, because «انْدَفَقَ الْمَاءُ» (the water gushed) is in the sense of «نَزَلَ» (it came down).

ukberi-tibyan:8-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّهُ عَلَى رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ (٨) يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ (٩)).
The hāʾ in «رَجْعِهِ» refers back to man, so the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object; i.e. Allah is able to resurrect him. On this view, there are several aspects regarding the words of the Exalted «يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ»: the first is that it is governed by «قَادِرٌ». The second is that it is by way of clarification (tabyīn), i.e. «يَرْجِعُ يَوْمَ تُبْلَى» (he returns on the day [secrets] are tested). The third is that its implied form is «اذْكُرْ» (remember). It is not permissible that «رَجْعِهِ» govern it, because of the separation between them by the khabar (predicate).
It is also said that the hāʾ in «رَجْعِهِ» is for the water; i.e. able to return the water into the urethra or into the loins. On this view it is cut off from the words of the Exalted «يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ», and «اذْكُرْ» (remember) governs it.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿إنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ﴾: its meaning is ”لَعَلَيْها حافِظٌ“ ("there is surely over it a guardian"), and ”ما“ is redundant (laghw). It was also read ”لَمّا عَلَيْها حافِطٌ“ with the doubled mīm (tashdīd), and then the meaning is the meaning of ”إلّا“ ("except"). ”لَمّا“ is used in the place of ”إلّا“ in two places: one of them is this, and the other is in the chapter of the oath; one says: ”سَألْتُكَ لَمّا فَعَلْتَ“ ("I ask you, by God, but that you do it"), meaning ”إلّا فَعَلْتَ“. [Translator's note: the source prints «حافِطٌ» with ṭāʾ in the second reading; this is evidently a misprint for «حافِظٌ».]

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خُلِقَ مِن ماءٍ دافِقٍ﴾ ("he was created from a gushing water"): its meaning is "from [what is] above" [Translator's note: so in the source, «مِن فَوْقَ»; it may be a corruption, e.g. of «مَدْفُوقٍ», "poured out"]. The doctrine of Sībawayh and his followers is that its meaning is attribution (nasab) to gushing; the meaning is ”مِن ماءِ ذِي انْدِفاقٍ“ ("from a water possessing gushing").

zajjaj:7-7.t:
And His saying: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِن بَيْنِ الصُّلْبِ والتَّرائِبِ﴾ ("it emerges from between the backbone and the tarāʾib"). ”اَلتَّرائِبُ“: it has come in the exegesis (tafsīr) that they are four ribs on the right side of the chest and four ribs on the left side of the chest; and it has come in the exegesis that the tarāʾib are the two hands, the two legs and the two eyes. The lexicographers all said: ”اَلتَّرائِبُ“ is the place of the necklace on the chest, and they recited for Imruʾ al-Qays:
مُهَفْهَفَةٌ بَيْضاءُ غَيْرُ مُفاضَةٍ ∗∗∗ تَرائِبُها مَصْقُولَةٌ كالسَّجَنْجَلِ
(Slender-waisted, fair, not flabby-bellied; her breastbones [tarāʾib] polished like a mirror.)

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ عَلى رَجْعِهِ لَقادِرٌ﴾ ("He is surely able to return it"): it has come in the exegesis: He is surely able to return the water to the urethra; and it has also come: to return it to the backbone; and it has also come: to return him, i.e. to resurrect the human being. This last is supported by His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تُبْلى السَّرائِرُ﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 9] ("the Day when secrets are put to the test"), that is: He is able to resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:11-12.t:
And His saying: ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ الرَّجْعِ﴾ ﴿والأرْضِ ذاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾: ”ذاتِ الرَّجْعِ“ means "possessing rain", because it comes, returns and recurs. Abū ʿUbayda said: ”اَلرَّجْعُ“ is water, and he recited the verse of al-Munakhkhal al-Hudhalī:
أبْيَضُ كالرَّجْعِ رَسُوبٌ إذا ∗∗∗ ما ثاخَ في مُحْتَفَلٍ يَخْتَلِي
(White like water [al-rajʿ], deep-sinking; when it plunges into the thick of a body it cuts through.)
He said: he is describing the sword; he says: it is white like water.
﴿والأرْضِ ذاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾: that is, it splits open with vegetation.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿إنَّهُ لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ﴾ ("it is surely a decisive word"): this is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam). By it the Qur'an is meant; it decides between truth and falsehood.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَما هو بِالهَزْلِ﴾: it is not frivolous play (laʿib).

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿إنَّهم يَكِيدُونَ كَيْدًا﴾ ("they are plotting a plot"): He means by it the unbelievers: that they practise deceit against the Prophet, peace be upon him, and display the opposite of what they are.

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿وَأكِيدُ كَيْدًا﴾ ("and I am plotting a plot"): Allah's plotting against them is His drawing them on step by step (istidrāj) from where they do not know.

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْهِلْهم رُوَيْدًا﴾: that is, give them respite for a little while.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ṭāriq
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿والسَّماءِ والطّارِقِ﴾: the answer to the oath is: ﴿إنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 4]. «اَلطّارِقُ» is the star, and by «اَلنَّجْمُ» (the star) the stars are meant. The star is called «طارِقٌ» (night-comer) only because its rising is at night, and everything that comes by night is a ṭāriq, because the night is a time in which one is still. From this it is said «أطْرَقَ فُلانٌ» when someone refrains from speaking and is still.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And ﴿الثّاقِبُ﴾ is the shining one. One says «ثَقَبَ، يَثْقُبُ، ثُقُوبًا» when it shines, and one says to the one kindling a fire: «أثْقِبْ نارَكَ», that is: make it blaze.
